$comment: How the keyboard row's buttons behave, replayed by the Android KeyRowTest and the Apple KeyRowTests. A button is a row id of the overlay_actions blob. Each case runs `steps` on a fresh row and expects `out` in order. Steps: ["tap", id]; ["hold", id] a long press begins; ["lift", id] that finger is gone; ["type", text] typed on the system keyboard toward a host that takes text, while a modifier is latched; ["release"] the keyboard hid or the stream ended. Out: "+11" and "-11" are a key down and up by its virtual-key code in hex; "text:hello" is committed text; "fire:<phase>:<id>" hands a quick action to the client's shortcut path, phase once, tap, down or up. `typed` maps a character to the key it presses under a latched modifier, null for one that goes as text. Hand-written: a new rule adds a case here first.

cases.name: a modifier holds until the next key lifts
a second tap lets the modifier go
release lets every modifier go once
a long press holds a key until the finger lifts
a tapped key goes down and up, and a lift after a tap sends nothing
a long-pressed modifier latches like a tapped one
a key name is read as key_vk reads it, alias and case
a character typed under a modifier goes as its key
a capital typed under a modifier is the same key, with no shift
tab typed under a modifier is the tab key, never text
text with no key goes as text once the modifier is up
a key combination is the next key
a held key combination comes up with the finger and lets the modifier go
any other action fires once and leaves the modifier held
the guide button holds like a key and is no key to a modifier
